manifest.description: Portable Git repository service and DSH client experience

bundle.text:
# Profile bundle: mount the portable Git service and client UI.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-plugin-git
      name: '@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git'

readme.text:
---
description: "Portable Git repository operations and Client UI for DeepSeek Harness Desktop and standard DSH Web profiles."
kind: "package-bundle"
---
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Standard DSH/Cordis Git plugin with one portable Host service, one Client bundle, and optional Desktop enhancement. The package runs unchanged in DeepSeek Harness Desktop and in a standard DSH Web host; the npm scope `@dsh-electron/` identifies the publisher, not a runtime requirement.

**Requires the upstream right sidebar.** Supported DSH releases are listed in the [compatibility contract](docs/reference/dsh-compatibility.md); their Client UI ships the right sidebar (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right`). Git registers three sidebar tab types through the standard two-stage path and navigates through `ctx.sidebarRight`; without the right sidebar the Client half cannot load. The third-party Details Host plugin is deprecated and no longer depended on. See the [DSH compatibility contract](docs/reference/dsh-compatibility.md) for the verified release list.

[DeepSeek Harness Desktop](https://github.com/cherrchen/deepseek-harness-electron) pre-installs this plugin and mirrors this repository with git subtree. Users may disable Git from the Plugins settings; the right sidebar is an upstream built-in.

See the [compatibility contract](docs/reference/dsh-compatibility.md) for the exact verified releases, development pin, host Node requirements, and candidate upgrade process.

The package is published to npm as `@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git` (current `0.2.9`, MIT, with build provenance). It is still experimental development: the API and versioning remain pre-1.0 and may change between minor releases.

**DeepSeek Harness Desktop** — Git is pre-installed and enabled by default. Disable it from **Settings → Plugins** when you do not need repository UI.

**DSH Web** — every supported release ships the right sidebar, so Git alone is enough. The shortest path is two commands:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git
dsh --profile web
```

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory: it installs the package and activates the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` layer that mounts the plugin. Four install sources are supported, shown here with the `web` profile:

| Source | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm registry (recommended) | `dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git` | Prebuilt artifact; no build authorization |
| tarball | `dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-electron-dsh-plugin-git-<version>.tgz` | Prebuilt offline package; no build authorization |
| local path | `dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-plugin-git` | pnpm links the checkout; for development |
| GitHub / git | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git` | Fetches sources and builds them on install through `prepare`; needs `allowBuilds`, pin a tag |

Whichever source you use, the Git client requires the host to already provide the `ctx.sidebarRight` and `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` services at load time; every supported DeepSeek Harness release provides them.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git
```

The registry holds the prebuilt artifact, so no package code runs on your machine at install time.

```sh
pnpm pack --pack-destination dist
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dist/dsh-electron-dsh-plugin-git-0.2.9.tgz
```

`pnpm pack` produces that single tarball, and every tag's GitHub Release carries the same one — for `0.2.9`, `https://github.com/cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git/releases/download/v0.2.9/dsh-electron-dsh-plugin-git-0.2.9.tgz`. It is prebuilt as well, which makes it the form to use for an offline or air-gapped profile.

A git install fetches **sources, not built artifacts**, so the package's own `prepare` script builds the published entry points on your machine: `pnpm run build` emits the declarations with `tsc` and then bundles both faces with `tsdown`, using only this package's standalone tsconfigs, so no sibling checkout is assumed. pnpm ≥ 10 refuses to run that script until it is explicitly allowed, so the first `add` fails with `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Copy the exact key pnpm prints into the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — for a git-hosted dependency that key is the package name plus the resolved git spec and commit, and a bare package name does not match it:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  # the key pnpm printed
  '@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git@git+<host>/<path>#<commit>': true
```

then run the `add` again. Moving the pin moves the commit, so the key moves with it. Treat that allowance as **permission for the package to execute code on your machine at install time**, outside any sandbox the agent runs under. Pin a tag so a later push cannot silently change what runs:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git#v0.2.9
```

```sh git clone https://github.com/cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git.git cd dsh-plugin-git pnpm install pnpm build # writes lib/, which Git ignores but the install reads pnpm links the checkout, so a later `pnpm build` is picked up without reinstalling. > **Note**: if your DSH is a source checkout rather than a global install, `dsh` is not on `PATH` — replace `dsh` with `pnpm dsh` in every command above, for example `pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add …`.

readme.section: Pairing with the upstream right sidebar
Pairing with the upstream right sidebar
readme.text: **Stage one** — `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(definition)` registers three tab types: `git.changes` and `git.graph` are page types (opened by kind, one tab per pane) that each contribute one guide entry (Changes `order: 11`, Graph `order: 12`), replacing the old Details launcher cards on the guide page; `git.diff` is a resource type with pattern `dsh-resource://git/diff/**`, a `canOpen` that validates the address decodes, and a title taken from the decoded file name. Optional Worktrees and Remote entries use orders 13 and 14, keeping all Git entries between Workspace files (10) and New terminal (20). Graph uses commit-lane artwork; Remote uses a cloud with upload/download arrows.

readme.section: Pairing with the upstream right sidebar
readme.text:
**Stage two** — each type's body component injects the `sidebar.right.pane.tab` seat under the definition's `id`; bodies read `{ address, params, revision }` from `useTabInfo().tab.navigation`.

Unified navigation converges on `ctx.sidebarRight`:

```text
ctx.sidebarRight.openTab('git.changes')
ctx.sidebarRight.openResource('dsh-resource://git/diff/<encodeURIComponent(path)>/<staged|worktree>', { params: { path, staged } })
ctx.sidebarRight.openTab('git.graph')
```

readme.section: Pairing with the upstream right sidebar
readme.text: A diff tab's identity is its exact address: re-opening the same file and comparison side reveals the existing tab and bumps its `revision` (the body refetches on it), while a staged and a working-tree diff of one file are two addresses and sit side by side. Changes and Graph dedupe per pane by kind, owned by the sidebar. The changed-files indicator, the branch chip, and the guide entries open `git.changes`; clicking a file row opens the `git.diff` for that path.

readme.section: Pairing with the upstream right sidebar

readme.text: In the conversation composer, Git contributes a branch selector and a changed-files indicator on the left of the input area. Clicking either control opens `git.changes` as a right-sidebar tab. Creating a branch opens a shared conversation Modal; after `git init` with no commits (unborn HEAD), the menu shows the symbolic default branch as disabled, explains that the first commit is required, and disables create until HEAD exists.

The selector follows that session's effective directory. Hosts that publish a `workingDirectory` session projection use it; otherwise Git keeps the session header directory. Each session has its own repository state. A linked checkout shows a worktree label. The Changes surface lists the repository's other checkouts. **Use in this session** appears only when the host can change that session's directory, and it asks the host working-directory service to enter the selected checkout; a **Manage worktrees** action opens the dedicated Worktrees tab while that tab is enabled. This package does not delete or prune worktrees.

The **Changes** surface shows the current branch beside refresh, then a single-line auto-growing commit message field with a wand **Generate** control and a split **Commit** button (Commit, Amend, Commit & Push, Commit & Sync). Staged, unstaged, and untracked paths follow as icon-action sections: plus or minus toggles the index, undo discards after a two-step confirm, and a porcelain letter badges the row. Clicking a path opens the matching diff. The **Diff** adapter shows refresh in the top-right and supplies one file's working-tree or staged comparison to the official DSH `DiffBlock`, which owns copying, folding, and line wrapping where supported. Git patch conversion and non-text states are described in the [architecture overview](docs/architecture/overview.md); the original resource addresses remain restorable. The **Graph** surface shows Auto / All / First parent beside refresh, then the commit history as a canvas-drawn lane graph — one continuous coordinate space, so rails and merge edges never break at row boundaries — each commit a single line of subject, author, and kind-colored HEAD/branch/remote/tag ref chips, with a hover card carrying the full subject, hash, author, da

The Host plugin requires `ctx.subprocess`, provides `ctx.git`, and starts Git with an executable plus separate argv values. It never invokes a shell. When a DSH Web Host is present, an optional Connection child registers the loopback `/git` RPC channel.

The Client plugin requires Connection, locale, renderer, conversation UI, primitives, session UI, and the upstream right sidebar (`ctx.sidebarRight` / `ctx.sidebarRightTabs`, type-only imports). Business components receive the controller for their session and `openDetails()` through slot injection and do not access Cordis context. Two sessions do not share one repository snapshot.

When `ctx.settingsScope` or `ctx.configForms` is present, the Client registers the commit-message and worktrees configuration sections through [`src/compat/dsh-client-settings.ts`](src/compat/dsh-client-settings.ts). `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.1.6-alpha.1` consume `settings.plugin.item` under the `git-commit-message` and `git-worktrees` namespaces, on **Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration**. From `0.1.6-alpha.2`, hosts consume `plugins.bundle.config` with a single card keyed by package name `@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git`, on that bundle's detail page between its description and its rows. From 0.1.7 the form data is the patch row id `dsh-plugin-git`, not the package name. The configuration is absent when the host declares neither slot or does not serve that namespace.

The Client main fiber does not require `desktop`. A child `ctx.inject(['desktop'], ...)` fiber accepts only `shell.showItemInFolder`, `shell.openPath`, and `notification.show`; without them, repository, status, diff, stage, commit, and branch operations remain available and native actions are not shown. No runtime invariant companion is published because Cordis owns the service, RPC registration, and child-fiber lifetimes this package uses.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `executable` | `git` | Git executable name or absolute path resolved by `ctx.subprocess`. |
| `maxOutputBytes` | 8 MiB | Per-stream collection cap for one Git command. |
| `graceMs` | 3000 | Managed subprocess termination grace period. |
| `commitMessage.provider` | — | Provider route registered with the DSH LLM runtime. Required when `commitMessage.mode` is `custom`. |
| `commitMessage.model` | — | Model id resolved by the provider route. Required when `commitMessage.mode` is `custom`. |
| `commitMessage.mode` | inherit | `inherit` uses the host session model; `custom` pins `provider`/`model`. |
| `commitMessage.systemPrompt` | built-in | System prompt for commit-message generation. Empty/absent uses the package default. |
| `commitMessage.maxDiffBytes` | 48 KiB | Staged-diff byte cap applied before the generation prompt is built (validated minimum 1024). |
| `worktrees.enabled` | — | Follow the host's upstream `worktrees` runtime by default; set `true` to enable the local implementation when none is mounted. |
| `worktrees.directory` | `.agents/worktrees` | Checkout pool for locally created worktrees: relative to the repository root,

The whole `commitMessage` section is optional and is also the `git-commit-message` settings namespace; likewise `worktrees` is the `git-worktrees` settings namespace. Edit either from the plugin configuration entry above, or as a composition entry. When the host exposes no LLM runtime, or no session model and no custom route resolve, commit message generation is unavailable and the Client reports `git/generation-unavailable`.

The first release supports repository discovery, Git version, current branch and HEAD, staged/unstaged/untracked status, local branches, working and staged diffs, stage/unstage, commit, amend, push to `origin`, rebase-then-push sync, branch creation, and branch switching. Status uses porcelain v2 with NUL path separators; branches use `for-each-ref`; every caller-supplied path, branch, and message remains one argv value. Status also records whether the checkout is the main worktree, a linked worktree, or bare, and lists checkouts with `git worktree list --porcelain`. Entering another checkout changes that session's directory through the host working-directory service and only accepts a path from that list. Creating a checkout goes through the host's experimental `worktrees` runtime when mounted — which also enters the new checkout — or through this plugin's own `git worktree add -b` when the `git-worktrees` `enabled` setting is on; deleting and pruning worktrees stay outside this package.

Discard restores one staged, unstaged, or untracked change, including an addition or rename edited after staging, through explicit index, worktree, and clean operations. It is destructive: the Client always asks for a second, explicit confirmation before sending the RPC, and the surface names the path in the confirm body.

Commit history is read with a paged `git log` (`GIT_LOG_FORMAT`, one commit per line, fixed field count) so the Graph surface appends older commits incrementally through a scroll sentinel instead of materializing the whole history.

Commit message generation is opt-in at the host: it needs an LLM runtime and a resolvable model (the session default, or a custom `provider`/`model`). A staged diff (capped by `commitMessage.maxDiffBytes`) is sent to that route and the streamed suggestion is written into the editable commit message input. The system prompt defaults to a Conventional Commit instruction and can be overridden from Plugin configuration. Generation is suggestion-only — it never stages, commits, or pushes anything.

GitHub Remote is available when the host provides the complete optional credentials seam: authentication, PR/Issue browsing, comparisons, PR comments/reviews, verified checkout, Issue branches, and guarded create/close/merge. See the [remote RPC contract](docs/reference/remote-platform-rpc.en.md) for configuration, limits, credential handling and unknown-result recovery, and the [active plan](docs/plans/active/remote-platform-integration.en.md) for acceptance evidence and unverified external scenarios. Git fetch/push uses existing Git transport credentials, independently of platform login. Stash, cherry-pick and merge-conflict editing remain outside this package.

The package is published to npm as `@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git` (MIT; latest `0.2.9`). Releases are cut by pushing a `vX.Y.Z` tag: the workflow runs the tests and build, packs the tarball, publishes it to npm with build provenance, and attaches the same tarball to a GitHub Release. API and versioning remain pre-1.0. The UI host is the upstream built-in right sidebar; no separately installed third-party pairing package is required. Release steps and credentials are documented in [`docs/development/README.en.md`](docs/development/README.en.md#release-process).

None. Commit-message generation is an independent Host LLM request and does not add, replace, or retain session tokens.

- **Independent Git transport** — Remote platform login does not configure Git fetch/push credentials; existing helpers or SSH remain responsible for Git authentication.
- **Bounded command output** — a diff larger than `maxOutputBytes` retains only the subprocess collector's tail, so deployments handling very large diffs must raise that validated setting.
- **Generation needs host + model** — commit message generation requires a host LLM runtime and a resolvable model (session default or a custom route in Plugin configuration); without either, the Generate action stays disabled or reports `git/generation-unavailable`.
- **Worktree entry needs a live directory service** — without the host working-directory service, or without a live agent for that session, the checkout list stays read-only. Writes then keep the previous caller-supplied repository contract. A missing directory is not repaired here; recovery belongs to the host working-directory service.
